label: Ricci Curvature
notes: Welcome to Chapter 14, the keystone of Part II spanning printed pages 357 through 420. Ricci curvature is the single scalar field that optimal transport will eventually replace with a synthetic definition. Today we build the bridge: from the averaged sectional curvature of smooth Riemannian geometry to convexity of entropy along displacement interpolation.

label: From Sectional to Ricci
notes: Sectional curvature lives on a plane; it tells you how two geodesics in that plane converge or diverge. Ricci curvature averages sectional curvature over all planes containing a fixed direction. So Ricci in direction v measures the net focusing felt by a whole transverse bundle of geodesics travelling alongside v.

label: Geodesic Deviation and Jacobi Fields
notes: A Jacobi field is the infinitesimal separation between neighbouring geodesics. Its acceleration obeys the Jacobi equation, governed by the curvature operator. Positive curvature makes the separation accelerate inward, focusing the family; negative curvature drives it apart. This is the mechanical heart of every curvature estimate in the chapter.

label: The Bochner Formula
notes: Bochner's identity is the analytic engine. It expresses the Laplacian of half the squared gradient as the Hessian norm plus a gradient-of-Laplacian term plus a Ricci term acting on the gradient. The Ricci term is exactly where curvature enters analysis, and it is what makes lower Ricci bounds controllable through inequalities.

label: Volume Distortion of a Ball
notes: Track a small geodesic ball as it flows along geodesics. Its volume changes at a rate set by Ricci curvature. Positive Ricci compresses the ball faster than flat space, negative Ricci lets it swell. The Jacobian of the exponential map is the bookkeeping device, and its determinant is the volume the gas must occupy.

label: Distortion Coefficients
notes: Distortion coefficients package a Ricci lower bound K together with a dimension upper bound N into explicit comparison functions. They interpolate the volume of intermediate points along a geodesic against the flat reference. The notebook orders the positive, zero, and negative curvature curves and checks numerically that small-distance behaviour matches the sign of curvature.

label: The Lazy Gas Experiment
notes: Here is Villani's signature heuristic. A gas of particles must redistribute itself from one density to another at least cost. Along the optimal displacement interpolation it passes through intermediate configurations. In positive curvature the geodesics focus, so the gas can momentarily occupy lower-volume, lower-entropy states. The gas is lazy and exploits that focusing.

label: Entropy Along Displacement
notes: Translate laziness into a formula. The Boltzmann entropy evaluated along the displacement interpolation is more convex when Ricci is larger. A lower bound Ric at least K g forces a quantitative convexity inequality for the entropy functional. This is the reformulation that turns a tensor statement into a statement about a functional on probability measures.

label: Lower Ricci Equals Entropy Convexity
notes: State the equivalence cleanly. On a smooth manifold, Ric greater than or equal to K g holds if and only if relative entropy is K-displacement-convex along every Wasserstein geodesic. The forward direction uses Bochner and Jacobi fields; the converse recovers the tensor by probing with concentrated measures. Both readings describe the same curvature.

label: The Curvature-Dimension Condition
notes: Refine the bound by adding dimension. The condition CD(K,N) couples a Ricci lower bound K with a dimension upper bound N through the distortion coefficients in the entropy inequality. It sharpens displacement convexity and, crucially, it is written entirely in transport language, so it survives where charts and tensors do not.

label: Bridge to Synthetic Geometry
notes: This is why the chapter sits at the centre of the book. Because CD(K,N) needs only a metric, a reference measure, and optimal transport, it can be taken as a definition on spaces with no smooth structure. Part III adopts exactly this as the synthetic notion of a lower Ricci bound for metric measure spaces.

label: Synthesis
notes: Recap the through-line. Ricci is averaged sectional curvature; Jacobi fields and Bochner make it control volume distortion; the lazy gas reads that distortion as entropy convexity along displacement interpolation; CD(K,N) packages curvature and dimension in pure transport terms; and that package becomes the synthetic definition of curvature in the chapters that follow.
